Process industries run on continuous physics: yields, energy and safety windows decided by process telemetry. Advanced process control plus predictive maintenance plus energy intelligence is the classic compounding stack — now with agentic planning on top.

items: Batch records, quality and ERP data disjoint; investigations slow and audits painful.
APC setpoints static while feedstock shifts; yield and energy losses accepted as normal.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Data Engineering & Pipeline Modernization, Real-Time Streaming & Event-Driven Decisioning, Master Data, Governance & Cataloging from the Data, Analytics & Lakehouse tower, wired into the unit's workflows (APC/advanced control, Predictive maintenance, Batch genealogy/investigation) on Dataq Forge and Dataq Nexus. Governance inherits the sector frame — IEC 62443 / ISA S84 among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: One customer, one product, one truth: MDM and catalog discipline that regulators can read.
Forward-looking risk on governed data: credit, insurance, operational and market models that explain themselves.
Turn the data estate into revenue: embedded analytics, data sharing and insight products with real P&L.
Batch/quality/ERP unified with lineage (investigations in hours)

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Manufacturing & Industrial level this capability reads as: meter-level energy analytics with per-unit cost and ESG feeds (energy cost per unit down 10-20%). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

The rhythm is fixed on purpose: progress becomes visible from week one, not after the first steering meeting. Weeks 1–2 are measurement only: we lock the current metric with your team and both sides sign it before a line of build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver a bounded pilot — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a named control owner on your side. Weeks 9–12 turn what worked into runbooks, monitoring and enablement, then report the measured delta against the baseline. A missed gate means a documented stop-or-redirect decision, not a quiet extension.
